creatives.angle: Highlighting organic ingredient transparency and emotional connection by framing organic produce as quality ingredients to share with pets.
claims_used: Organic produce and pantry items delivered at up to 40% off supermarkets

issues: The seasonal reference ('this Halloween') makes the ad copy non-evergreen and irrelevant for most of the year.

Framing a standard human grocery delivery service as ingredients to 'share with your pet' is highly awkward and potentially dangerous, as many common produce and pantry items (e.g., onions, grapes, garlic, raisins, chocolate) are toxic to pets.

config.advertiser_summary: Organic produce and pantry items delivered via weekly or biweekly subscription boxes at up to 40% off supermarket prices, targeting budget-conscious and food-waste-aware households.

assumptions: Price not given; assumed $25 for a 'budget' product.
subscription: assumed 4.0 orders per customer over ~6 months.
Margin not given; assumed 40% (typical for groceries) for the break-even estimate only.
Break-even per customer (guidance, not enforced): $25 x 40% x 4.0 orders = $40.00.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click: verifiable without trusting a pixel. Maximise conversions within the budget: bids move between $0.25 and the $1.00 cap (category default) to spend it well; no CPA target is invented.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.

allocations.rationale: score 0.63, relative fit x1.40; 0.0640 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $0.70 (cap $1.00); host also sells this kind of product: confirm it allows competing brands, otherwise this budget reflows to the other hosts
score 0.41, relative fit x1.11; 0.0637 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $0.56 (cap $0.80)
score 0.27, relative fit x0.94; 0.0643 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $0.47 (cap $0.67)

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: fixed start bid per host; pacing only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded

phases.name: maximize
phases.rule: bid = start x pacing x conversion likelihood, within [floor, cap]: spend the budget on the best opportunities
phases.why: no CPA target was set, so the goal is the most units for the budget

adjustments.reason: Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.
Bid higher when the shopper looks like a likely converter (persona match vs the host's average shopper).

bid_strategy.rationale: Maximise conversions within the budget, never above the $1.00 cap (category default).
